assumptions: "Open pipeline" means opportunities where is_closed = false (and is_deleted = false).

SELECT * FROM dated_conversion_rates LIMIT 20;

SELECT o.id, o.currency_iso_code, o.close_date, o.arr__c
FROM opportunities o
JOIN users u ON o.owner_id = u.id

  AND o.close_date >= r.start_date AND o.close_date < r.next_start_date

WITH rates AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.arr__c, o.currency_iso_code, o.close_date,
    (SELECT r.conversion_rate FROM dated_conversion_rates r
     WHERE r.iso_code = o.currency_iso_code AND r.start_date <= o.close_date

results.trap: 'best quarter' = new ARR, total ARR, or deal count
assumptions: 'Best quarter' is measured by closed-won revenue (new ARR and total deal amount) from the opportunities table, since that's the primary revenue-generating metric.
'This year' refers to 2026 (current year, today = 2026-09-11).
Amounts were converted to USD using the dated_conversion_rates table to fairly compare deals booked in USD, GBP, and CAD.

Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) is only partially complete (through Sep 11) so it's naturally lower and excluded from being 'best' despite being in progress; Q2 2026 (Apr-Jun) had the highest closed-won ARR (~$4.46M) and total deal amount (~$5.1M) among the two complete quarters (Q1 and Q2) plus the partial Q3.
Value submitted (2) represents Q2 (calendar quarter number) as the best quarter of 2026.
sqlQueries:
SELECT date_trunc('quarter', close_date)::date AS quarter, count(*) AS deals, sum(amount) AS total_amount, sum(arr__c) AS total_arr
FROM opportunities
WHERE is_won = true AND is_closed = true AND date_part('year', close_date) = 2026
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
SELECT currency_iso_code, count(*) FROM opportunities WHERE is_won=true AND is_closed=true AND date_part('year', close_date)=2026 GROUP BY 1;

WITH o AS (
  SELECT o.*, date_trunc('quarter', o.close_date)::date AS q
  FROM opportunities o
  WHERE o.is_won = true AND o.is_closed = true AND date_part('year', o.close_date) = 2026
),
rates AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.q, o.amount, o.arr__c, o.currency_iso_code,
    (SELECT conversion_rate FROM dated_conversion_rates dcr
     WHERE dcr.iso_code = o.currency_iso_code
       AND dcr.start_date <= o.close_date
       AND (dcr.next_start_date IS NULL OR dcr.next_start_date > o.close_date)
     LIMIT 1) AS rate
  FROM o
)
SELECT q, count(*) AS deals,
  sum(amount / COALESCE(rate,1)) AS amount_usd,
  sum(arr__c / COALESCE(rate,1)) AS arr_usd
FROM rates
GROUP BY q
ORDER BY q;
